# Retail CoD 1.1d dedicated server trigger notifies under a walking client.
# map mp_pavlov, g_gametype probe_trigger (whose main() calls
# maps\mp\gametypes\dm::main()), joined allies, dedicated 1, sv_maxclients 8,
# sv_pure 0, stock scr_* defaults, one client on the server. Captured 2026-09-08.
# The evidence is the server's own games_mp.log, not a client capture: the
# gametype is crates/gsc/tests/fixtures/semantics/client-probes/probe_trigger.gsc,
# which threads a waittill("trigger", other) onto every trigger entity the map
# spawned and logPrints one line per notify.
#
# Two shells:
#   COD_LNXDED_HOME=<absolute path with no '+' in it> SECS=420 \
#       tools/run_probe.sh client-probes/probe_trigger mp_pavlov
#   cargo run -p vcod -- --net-probe 127.0.0.1:28970 --probe-triggers \
#       --probe-team allies --probe-secs 395
#
# PROBE watch <entity> <classname> is the census: every trigger entity that
# survived the gametype's _gameobjects pass, in the order getEntArray returned
# them. dm claims no gameobjects, so the five entities carrying a
# script_gameobjectname are deleted and are not here: three trigger_multiples
# (bombzone_B *2, bombzone_A *3 and auto2 *34, the last a "re" retrieval zone),
# the trigger_lookat and the trigger_use. What is left is the 26 minefield
# trigger_multiples and the map's one trigger_hurt.
#
# PROBE fire <entity> <classname> <toucher entity> <toucher origin> is one
# notify. None of the minefield triggers carries a wait or a random key, so
# retail fires on every touch pass while the player stands in one, which is why
# one crossing is a run of lines rather than a single one; the origin on each
# line is the toucher's at that pass.
#
# The route: --probe-triggers steers at the map's trigger brushes in turn,
# nearest first, and kills itself when it wedges, so the run is a series of
# walks out of whatever spawn the last death gave it. This one crossed six of
# them -- entities 83, 93, 98, 101, 102 and 202 -- and died 14 times doing it,
# each death a minefield the walk stood in. The remaining twenty sit behind the
# town's solid geometry and cannot be walked into; the census covers all 27
# entities either way, and it is the census plus the origins here that the gate
# replays, never the walk.
#
# What this does NOT evidence: the trigger_hurt at entity 72 fired zero times.
# Its brush is the kill volume under the map's floor and a walking player never
# reaches it, so every line here comes from a trigger_multiple. Nothing in this
# file says anything about the hurt cadence, the damage a hurt deals or the
# spawnflag that slows it; entity 72 is evidenced as existing and as surviving
# the gametype's deletion pass, and no further.
PROBE watch 83 trigger_multiple
